note: Three anti-GM-CSF ligand antibodies entered RA on the mouse CIA/SCW-arthritis prediction: namilumab met DAS28-CRP in Phase 2, otilimab beat placebo on ACR20 in two Phase 3 trials but missed its Phase 2b remission primary and the targeted-therapy-IR Phase 3 and was dropped in 2022, and lenzilumab's RA trial stopped after 9 patients; the alveolar proteinosis the GM-CSF-null mouse predicted never appeared. Mavrilimumab blocks the receptor, is not a member and is not scored.
label: Rheumatoid arthritis (anti-GM-CSF)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The mouse studies used the anti-mouse GM-CSF surrogate mAb 22E9; the human antibodies bind human and macaque GM-CSF only (Krinner 2007, 10.1016/j.molimm.2006.03.020), so product_in_model is false.
engagement.model: Mouse collagen-induced and streptococcal cell wall arthritis, anti-GM-CSF mAb 22E9
engagement.quote: By histology, both inflammation and cartilage destruction were reduced in anti-GM-CSF-treated mice, and the levels of tumor necrosis factor-a and IL-1beta were also reduced in joint tissue washouts of these mice.
engagement.note: Model PD readouts were joint-washout TNF and IL-1beta; no anti-GM-CSF trial has measured joint cytokines in patients.
engagement.short: Joint TNF/IL-1beta readouts, no human comparison
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at first antibody use. Genovese 2020 found no change in 110 of 112 serum biomarkers (IL-6, MMP-3 among them), but serum markers are not the joint-washout readout the mouse used, so no comparison is admissible on this track.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Academic (Hamilton lab) model run with anti-mouse GM-CSF and gene-deleted mice, not with any member antibody.
engagement.model: Mouse GM-CSF-IRF4-CCL17 pathway in zymosan/antigen arthritis pain models
engagement.quote: In murine models of arthritis and pain, IRF4 regulated the formation of CCL17, which mediated the proinflammatory and algesic actions of GM-CSF.
engagement.note: Mouse arthritis and pain models put CCL17 downstream of GM-CSF, naming a circulating PD readout; Cook 2018 extended it to established arthritis.
engagement.short: CCL17 named as GM-CSF PD readout
engagement.judgement: Separate track from the CIA/SCW efficacy models: a different system (pathway and pain models) making a different prediction (a downstream PD marker and pain relief), per the track-identity rule for this run.

engagement.magnitude_basis: serum CCL17 ratio to baseline 0.65-0.68 at weeks 2-8 on otilimab 180 mg versus mouse Ccl17 ablation; not on a common scale
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Genovese 2020 (Lancet Rheumatol 2:e666-76); registry NCT02799472 results posted 2018-11-16 set the year. The paper is built on the Hamilton-lab axis but whether it puts mouse and patient CCL17 side by side is not visible from the abstract, so the comparison is paired by me. n=28 otilimab, 11 placebo.
engagement.model: Mouse GM-CSF-IRF4-CCL17 pathway in zymosan/antigen arthritis pain models
engagement.quote: CCL17 concentrations decreased from baseline to week 1, remained stable to week 8, and returned to baseline at week 12; least-squares mean ratio to baseline was 0·65 (95% CI 0·49-0·86; coefficient of variation 13·60) at week 2
engagement.note: Otilimab cut serum CCL17 by about a third while GM-CSF-otilimab complex showed engagement; CCL17 rebounded at week 12 when every-other-week dosing lost engagement.
engagement.judgement: Scored downstream: CCL17 is a chemokine two steps below the target, not the target's own product. The rebound at week 12 tracks the loss of engagement rather than contradicting the pathway, so it is a match in direction; the pain prediction of the same model (BAROQUE pain PROs improved) is a secondary endpoint and is noted, not scored.
engagement.reason: Mouse PD marker moved in dosed patients

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Koch 2012 (10.1007/s10928-011-9230-4) later fitted a PK/PD model to 22E9 at 0.1-100 mg/kg in CIA mice with a GM-CSF compartment driving disease; it states no human exposure target.
dose.model: Mouse collagen-induced and streptococcal cell wall arthritis, anti-GM-CSF mAb 22E9
dose.quote: DBA/1 mice were immunized for the development of CIA and treated at different times, and with different doses, with neutralizing mAb to GM-CSF or isotype control mAb.
dose.note: Mouse dosing was mg/kg of a surrogate antibody; the implied target is sustained GM-CSF neutralisation, with no human exposure number stated.
dose.short: Surrogate mg/kg doses, target is neutralisation
dose.judgement: Opening entry at first antibody use. Plater-Zyberk 2007 (SCW) found 22E9 dose-related at 100-300 ug/mouse and comparable to dexamethasone; the knockout gene-dosage effect (Campbell 1998) implies near-complete neutralisation is needed.

dose.magnitude_basis: dosing interval: the weekly-then-every-other-week regimen used in the Phase 2a/2b lost GM-CSF-otilimab complex and CCL17 suppression by week 12; Phase 3 doubled the maintenance frequency to weekly 90/150 mg
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Genovese 2020 and Buckley 2020 (both Lancet Rheumatol, 2020-10-07). BAROQUE (NCT02504671, results posted 2019-04-04) used the same weekly x5 then every-other-week regimen at 22.5-180 mg and missed its primary at every dose; the paper itself calls the exposure suboptimal. The model side (Koch 2012) is a mouse PK/PD model whose premise is sustained neutralisation, not a human exposure number, so the pairing is mine.
dose.model: Mouse collagen-induced and streptococcal cell wall arthritis, anti-GM-CSF mAb 22E9
dose.quote: Serum concentrations of GM-CSF-otilimab complex indicated that target engagement was achieved with initial weekly dosing, but not sustained with every other week dosing.
dose.note: The Phase 2a/2b regimen under-dosed the target: engagement and CCL17 suppression were lost on every-other-week maintenance, and BAROQUE missed its primary at all five doses.
dose.short: Every-other-week regimen lost engagement; Phase 2b missed
dose.judgement: Dose-table row 'target never reached': the model's implied target (sustained neutralisation) was not held on every-other-week maintenance, the regimen the class went into Phase 2b on, so dose is contra and BAROQUE efficacy untested; magnitude is the roughly 2x change in dosing frequency Phase 3 adopted. No tolerability margin was stated by the mouse, and no toxicity limited the human dose.

dose.confidence_note: Protocol Amendment 02 (approved 2020-01-21), uploaded to ClinicalTrials.gov 2023-01-31; a registry-hosted document, scored tier 3. The GLP studies are unpublished and predate the protocol (the 26-week study had to precede BAROQUE's 50-week dosing), so 2020 is the earliest public date, not the first use. NOEL 5 mg/kg; dose levels and exposures sit in the Investigator Brochure, which is not public.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13-week SC and 26-week IV GLP toxicology of otilimab (GSK3196165)
dose.quote: The highest dose of 150 mg weekly provides a 3 to 5-fold safety margin to the 5 mg/kg dose in the 26-week monkey toxicology study where no foamy alveolar macrophages were observed (NOEL).
dose.note: Sponsor's dose rationale: 150 mg weekly sits 3-5-fold below the 26-week monkey NOEL for foamy alveolar macrophages.
dose.short: Monkey NOEL margin stated for 150 mg
dose.judgement: Own track: a different system (the product itself in a primate, GLP toxicology) making a different prediction (a tolerability margin for the clinical dose) from the arthritis mice (efficacy exposure) and the knockout (unconditional PAP). Decision 16 scores this toxic end of the window; the efficacy end stays on the 22E9 track.

dose.population: RA with inadequate response to biologic DMARDs and/or JAK inhibitors, background csDMARD (contRAst 3)
dose.magnitude_basis: 150 mg weekly, the dose at the stated 3-5-fold margin, given for up to 24 weeks in contRAst 3 (549 treated across arms) with adverse-event incidence matching placebo and sarilumab; human exposures not reported in the paper
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 37696589, PMC10646837; registry NCT04134728 results 2023-07-17). The efficacy end of the dose rule (150 mg weekly missed ACR20 here) is scored on the 22E9 track; this entry scores only the tolerability margin (decision 16).
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13-week SC and 26-week IV GLP toxicology of otilimab (GSK3196165)
dose.quote: The incidence of adverse or serious adverse events was similar across treatment groups.
dose.note: contRAst 3 dosed 150 mg weekly, the dose the monkey margin covered, with adverse-event rates matching placebo and sarilumab.
dose.short: Stated margin held at 150 mg weekly
dose.judgement: Decision 16: the model stated the clinical dose was tolerated (NOEL margin) and patients were dosed to it without the lung toxicity, so dose is same with margin_stated. contRAst 1 and 2 (registry results 2023-10-25 and 2023-11-30) dosed the same regimen; contRAst 3 is the earliest public record.

dose.population: Long-term extension of contRAst 1-3 (methotrexate-, cs/bDMARD- and bDMARD/JAKi-inadequate responders)
dose.magnitude_basis: zero PAP and no lung finding of the monkey type reported in 2915 patients at 90/150 mg weekly for up to 896 days
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 40044198, PMC11883618; registry NCT04333147 results 2024-02-07, no quotable sentence there). The extension was cut short by the programme decision, so the margin was tested to 2.5 years, not lifelong.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13-week SC and 26-week IV GLP toxicology of otilimab (GSK3196165)
dose.quote: There were no instances of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), active tuberculosis (TB), TB reactivation or serious hypersensitivity reactions.
dose.note: contRAst X: no PAP over up to 2.5 years at the covered dose; the monkey margin held to the end of the programme.
dose.reason: Monkey NOEL margin held in patients
dose.judgement: Strengthens the 2023 call with the direct lung readout at 13x the exposure; the harm is still counted once, here in dose, per decision 16.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. GM-CSF-null mice were already protected from CIA in 1998 (Campbell, 10.4049/jimmunol.161.7.3639); the antibody system opens here. Plater-Zyberk 2007 (10.1136/ard.2006.057182) and 2009 (10.1136/ard.2007.085431) added SCW arthritis, where 22E9 worked and etanercept did not.
efficacy.model: Mouse collagen-induced and streptococcal cell wall arthritis, anti-GM-CSF mAb 22E9
efficacy.quote: Importantly, anti-GM-CSF mAb treatment ameliorated existing disease, seen both as a reduction in the number of initially affected limbs progressing and lower numbers of additional limbs becoming affected.
efficacy.note: 22E9 cleared established CIA and TNF-independent SCW arthritis (comparable to dexamethasone, better than etanercept); the model behind namilumab and otilimab.
efficacy.short: 22E9 clears CIA and TNF-independent SCW arthritis
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. The lenzilumab RA trial (NCT00995449, 9 patients, terminated 'program refocus', results posted 2012-09-25) and the MOR103 Phase 1b/2a (NCT01023256, safety primary) produced no primary-endpoint efficacy datum and change no status. Opens the namilumab sc track; the otilimab sc track starts at efficacy 3.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse clinical arthritis score vs DAS28-CRP; LS-mean difference -0.92 at 150 mg (p=0.010 registry, p=0.005 paper); not on a common scale
efficacy.population: RA with inadequate response to methotrexate or one TNF inhibitor, background methotrexate in both arms (NEXUS)
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry NCT02379091 (tier 3, results posted 2018-09-14) sets the year and carries the numbers; Taylor 2019 (Arthritis Res Ther 21:101) is abstract-level reading. Per-protocol analysis, n=108; 20 and 80 mg missed (p=0.086, 0.107).
efficacy.model: Mouse collagen-induced and streptococcal cell wall arthritis, anti-GM-CSF mAb 22E9
efficacy.quote: At week 12, a statistically significant difference in DAS28-CRP (p = 0.005) was seen for namilumab 150 mg versus placebo and separation was seen as early as week 2 for namilumab 150 mg (p < 0.05)
efficacy.note: NEXUS namilumab 150 mg: DAS28-CRP -1.69 vs -0.77 placebo at week 12 (difference -0.92, p=0.010), dose-responsive; the mouse prediction held in direction.
efficacy.short: Namilumab met DAS28-CRP primary at 150 mg

patient_trials.quote: Change From Baseline in DAS28-CRP at Week 12: placebo -0.77, namilumab 20 mg -1.38, 80 mg -1.36, 150 mg -1.69; LS mean difference vs placebo -0.61 (p=0.086), -0.60 (p=0.107), -0.92 (p=0.010).
MOR103 Phase 1b/2a: primary outcome safety; exploratory analyses showed significant DAS28 improvement at 1.0 and 1.5 mg/kg versus placebo (Behrens 2015).
KB003 (lenzilumab) in biologics-inadequate RA: 9 participants enrolled; the study was terminated upon completion of safety run-in due to program refocus.

efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: the trial paper does not cite the mouse comparison. First primary-endpoint comparison for the class; the MOR103 exploratory signal (2014) and the 9-patient lenzilumab run-in are listed but change no status.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: DAS28-CRP remission at week 24: 14-19% at 90-180 mg vs 3% placebo, best OR 8.39 (95% CI 0.98-72.14, p=0.053); primary not met at any dose
efficacy.population: RA with inadequate response to methotrexate, background methotrexate in both arms (BAROQUE)
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry NCT02504671 (tier 3, results posted 2019-04-04) sets the year and carries the odds ratios; Buckley 2020 (Lancet Rheumatol 2:e677-88) is abstract-level reading. Escape-to-180 mg design with escapers counted as non-responders, n=222.
efficacy.model: Mouse collagen-induced and streptococcal cell wall arthritis, anti-GM-CSF mAb 22E9
efficacy.quote: Otilimab plus methotrexate was well tolerated and, despite not achieving the primary endpoint of DAS28-CRP remission, there were improvements compared with placebo in disease activity scores.
efficacy.note: BAROQUE otilimab 22.5-180 mg every other week plus background methotrexate missed DAS28-CRP remission at week 24 at every dose (best 19% vs 3%, p=0.053); secondaries improved. Untested: the regimen did not hold target engagement (dose cell, target never reached), so the miss does not test the model.
efficacy.judgement: Adjudicated untested (check verdict efficacy 3): the primary was missed with significant secondaries and the authors call it neither match nor miss, and the dose table's 'target never reached' row (engagement lost on every-other-week maintenance, Genovese 2020) leaves efficacy untested. Add-on to background methotrexate in both arms, so not a combination trial.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: contRAst 3 ACR20 at week 12 in bDMARD/JAKi-IR: 45% (90 mg, p=0.2868) and 51% (150 mg, p=0.0596) vs 38% placebo; sarilumab 58% (p=0.0049)
efficacy.population: RA in contRAst 1-3 (methotrexate-, cs/bDMARD- and bDMARD/JAKi-inadequate responders), background csDMARD
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry NCT04134728 (tier 3, results posted 2023-07-17) sets the year and reproduces the ACR20 rates; Taylor 2023 (Ann Rheum Dis 82:1527-37) and Fleischmann 2023 (82:1516-26) are abstract-level reading. n=549 in contRAst 3; 1537 and 1625 in contRAst 1 and 2.
efficacy.model: Mouse collagen-induced and streptococcal cell wall arthritis, anti-GM-CSF mAb 22E9
efficacy.quote: Otilimab demonstrated an acceptable safety profile but failed to achieve the primary end point of ACR20 and improve secondary end points versus placebo or demonstrate non-inferiority to sarilumab in this patient population.
efficacy.note: contRAst 3 (bDMARD/JAKi-IR) missed ACR20 vs placebo and non-inferiority to sarilumab; contRAst 1 and 2 met ACR20 vs placebo but were inferior to tofacitinib. First public in GSK's 27 Oct 2022 release, which also ended the programme; scored contra on the contRAst 3 primary miss.
efficacy.short: Failed in targeted-therapy-IR; met ACR20 elsewhere

patient_trials.quote: ACR20 at Week 12: GSK3196165 90 mg 44.8%, 150 mg 50.7%, sarilumab 57.5%, pooled placebo 37.7%; OR vs placebo 1.38 (p=0.2868) and 1.75 (p=0.0596).
contRAst 1 (MTX-IR) ACR20 at Week 12: 90 mg 54.7% (p=0.0023), 150 mg 50.9% (p=0.0362), tofacitinib 63.6%, pooled placebo 42.7%.
contRAst 2 (cs/bDMARD-IR, global cohort) ACR20 at Week 12: 90 mg 54.9% and 150 mg 54.5% (both p<0.0001), tofacitinib 71.1%, pooled placebo 32.5%; Asia cohort terminated early.

efficacy.judgement: First contra on the otilimab sc track now that BAROQUE is untested. Rule 6: the GSK press release of 2022-10-27 ('Data from ContRAst-3 ... did not demonstrate statistical significance on the primary endpoint of ACR20') made the miss public before the registry (2023-07-17) and paper; the tier-1 paper keeps the src. contRAst 1/2 met their primaries (partial agreement, in patient_trials); the tofacitinib comparison was a superiority secondary, not a non-inferiority gate. Not neg: the mouse data never fell below the class bar.
efficacy.reason: Mouse TNF-refractory prediction failed in patients

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Stanley 1994 (10.1073/pnas.91.12.5592) reported the same lung pathology plus subclinical lung infections in an independent knockout; Kitamura 1999 (10.1084/jem.190.6.875) showed neutralising anti-GM-CSF autoantibodies cause human PAP, the loss-of-function analogue in people.
safety.quote: Although steady-state hematopoiesis was unimpaired in homozygous mutant animals, all animals developed the progressive accumulation of surfactant lipids and proteins in the alveolar space, the defining characteristic of the idiopathic human disorder pulmonary alveolar proteinosis.
safety.note: Germline GM-CSF loss gives every mouse alveolar proteinosis and lung infection; every anti-GM-CSF trial then monitored lung function, KL-6 and surfactant protein D.
safety.judgement: Own track: a different system (germline null) making a different prediction (a lung harm) from the antibody-treated arthritis mice. The antibody arthritis models were short-term and silent on safety. Opens the otilimab sc track; otilimab IV (MOR103) and namilumab sc have their own openers and comparisons appended.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of the 22E9 CIA and SCW papers; none reports a tolerability, infection or lung readout.
safety.model: Mouse collagen-induced and streptococcal cell wall arthritis, anti-GM-CSF mAb 22E9
safety.quote: Neither humoral nor cellular immunity to type II collagen, however, was affected by anti-GM-CSF mAb treatment.
safety.note: Short-term arthritis experiments reported efficacy only; intact collagen immunity is a mechanistic finding, not a safety prediction.
safety.judgement: No harm appeared in patients to test the silence: serious AE rates were similar across arms in all three contRAst trials and NEXUS saw no serious infections, so the cell stays untested rather than same. Lung harm is scored on the knockout track.

safety.magnitude_basis: predicted alveolar proteinosis and lung infection in every animal; no pulmonary event of clinical concern in 222 patients dosed up to 50 weeks
safety.population: RA with inadequate response to methotrexate, background methotrexate in both arms (BAROQUE)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Buckley 2020; registry NCT02504671 (results posted 2019-04-04) carries the AE tables but the explicit pulmonary statement is in the paper, which sets the year. Earlier RA trials (MOR103 2014, PRIORA 2017, NEXUS 2019) monitored lung function without reporting PAP but their abstracts do not say so in a quotable sentence. The knockout is complete, lifelong loss; antibody neutralisation was partial and short, so the mouse may still be right at full neutralisation.
safety.quote: There were no deaths or pulmonary events of clinical concern, and rates of serious infection were low.
safety.note: No alveolar proteinosis or lung infection signal in BAROQUE after up to 50 weeks of otilimab at 22.5-180 mg; the predicted harm did not appear.
safety.judgement: A predicted harm that never appeared is a wrong prediction under the v3 safety rule (contra, opposite). Counted here, not in dose: the model predicted the harm but no margin, and no toxicity blocked dosing. The caveat that the regimen under-engaged the target (dose cell) is why confidence is medium.

safety.magnitude_basis: predicted alveolar proteinosis in every animal; zero cases in 2915 patients exposed 7-896 days at weekly 90/150 mg
safety.population: Long-term extension of contRAst 1-3 (methotrexate-, cs/bDMARD- and bDMARD/JAKi-inadequate responders)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Weinblatt 2025 (BMJ Open, contRAst X, NCT04333147; registry results posted 2024-02-07). Exposure at the weekly regimen that held engagement, up to 2.5 years; the extension was cut short by the programme's termination, so lifelong exposure was never tested.
safety.quote: There were no instances of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), active tuberculosis (TB), TB reactivation or serious hypersensitivity reactions.
safety.note: contRAst X: no alveolar proteinosis, TB or serious hypersensitivity in 2915 otilimab-treated patients over up to 2.5 years at the weekly regimen.
safety.short: No PAP in 2915 patients over 2.5 years
safety.judgement: Strengthens the 2020 call at the regimen that held target engagement and over 13x the exposure; the knockout's second prediction (lung infection, Stanley 1994) also failed to appear. Still partial neutralisation, so the mouse is wrong for the antibody class as dosed, not necessarily for complete GM-CSF loss.
safety.reason: No PAP at sustained engagement, 2.5 years

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 10499925, PMC2195627). model_kind human_genetic is the nearest enum: the state is an acquired autoimmune loss of GM-CSF signalling, not a germline genotype. Uchida 2004 (10.1182/blood-2003-05-1565) showed the autoantibody neutralises lung GM-CSF 4000-58,000-fold in excess; Uchida 2009 (10.1182/blood-2008-05-155689; PubMed lists the DOI as blood-2009-05-155689, which redirects to it) defined the critical autoantibody threshold for PAP.
safety.model: Human anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (acquired loss of GM-CSF signalling)
safety.quote: We report here that I-PAP is an autoimmune disease with neutralizing antibody of immunoglobulin G isotype against granulocyte/macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF).
safety.note: Neutralising anti-GM-CSF autoantibodies in every idiopathic PAP patient: people, not mice, show what sustained GM-CSF neutralisation does to the lung.
safety.short: Human autoantibody PAP predicts lung harm
safety.judgement: Own track from the GM-CSF-null mouse: a different system (acquired antibody neutralisation in people) with a different prediction (PAP only above a neutralising threshold, Uchida 2009), and the one the RA trials cited when they chose SP-D, KL-6 and PFT monitoring (Behrens 2015 ref 21; NEXUS ref 32). Opens the otilimab IV track (MOR103); the namilumab sc and otilimab sc tracks start at safety 7 and 8.

safety.population: Active RA, Phase 1b/2a (MOR103 IV, four weekly doses; NCT01023256)
safety.magnitude_basis: serum SP-D and PFTs unchanged after four weekly IV doses of 0.3-1.5 mg/kg MOR103 (69 treated) against the model's threshold-conditional PAP prediction; depth of alveolar GM-CSF neutralisation not measured
safety.confidence_note: OA full text (PMC4431325; online 2014-02-17, registry NCT01023256 results first posted 2014-05-08). Four weeks of partial neutralisation cannot produce PAP on the model's own terms, so this first dataset tests only the conditional arm; no trial measured whether pharmacological neutralisation crossed the Uchida 2009 threshold (no BAL GM-CSF bioactivity).
safety.model: Human anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (acquired loss of GM-CSF signalling)
safety.quote: Surfactant D levels remained normal and there was no overall pattern of PFT alterations in MOR103-treated subjects.
safety.note: MOR103 Phase 1b/2a: SP-D and PFTs monitored because of autoantibody PAP; both normal after four weekly doses, as the threshold model predicts.
safety.short: No PAP surrogate rise, as predicted
safety.judgement: same, not contra: the human model predicts PAP only after prolonged, complete neutralisation above a critical autoantibody threshold (Uchida 2004, 2009), and the sponsor stated the same reading ('clinical onset of PAP requires prolonged and complete inhibition of GMCSF', contRAst 3 protocol, citing hereditary CSF2RA PAP). Normal SP-D and PFTs at partial four-week neutralisation agree with that prediction in direction, where the knockout's unconditional prediction is scored contra. comparison_stated true because Behrens names the autoantibody-PAP association as the reason for the readouts and reports them. Hinge for the adjudicator (rule question 5): if a conditional prediction is unscorable without measuring the condition this falls to untested; it turns contra only if neutralisation is shown to have crossed the threshold.

safety.population: RA with inadequate response to methotrexate or one TNF inhibitor, background methotrexate in both arms (NEXUS)
safety.magnitude_basis: CEA, KL-6 and SP-D without treatment trend over 12 weeks of namilumab 20-150 mg SC (81 treated); neutralisation depth unmeasured
safety.confidence_note: OA full text (PMC6471864). NEXUS monitored lungs 'because of the theoretical risk of developing pulmonary alveolar proteinosis when using therapeutic antibodies that target GM-CSF', citing the Japanese autoimmune-PAP cohort (Inoue 2008, 10.1164/rccm.200708-1271OC), so the human analogue is the stated model. Year follows the registry results posting (NCT02379091, 2018-09-14), as the draft dates this trial; the quotable sentence is in the 2019 paper.
safety.model: Human anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (acquired loss of GM-CSF signalling)
safety.quote: With regard to change from baseline in biomarkers with the potential for early detection of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (carcinoembryonic antigen, KL-6, and SP-D), there were no trends associated with namilumab treatment.
safety.note: NEXUS: no trend in CEA, KL-6 or SP-D over 12 weeks of namilumab; AEs suggestive of PAP adjudicated as other diagnoses.
safety.short: No PAP biomarker trend, second drug
safety.judgement: Second member drug, three times the exposure, same direction; still partial neutralisation, so it strengthens the conditional-arm agreement rather than testing the threshold. First comparison on the human-PAP namilumab sc track.

safety.population: Long-term extension of contRAst 1-3 (methotrexate-, cs/bDMARD- and bDMARD/JAKi-inadequate responders)
safety.magnitude_basis: zero PAP in 2915 patients on weekly 90/150 mg otilimab for 7-896 days; neutralisation depth unmeasured
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 40044198, PMC11883618). Registry NCT04333147 results posted 2024-02-07 carry AE tables but no quotable PAP sentence, so the paper dates the entry, as on the knockout track. Weekly dosing held CCL17 engagement, yet no trial measured alveolar GM-CSF bioactivity; the model's threshold remains the unmeasured condition.
safety.model: Human anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (acquired loss of GM-CSF signalling)
safety.quote: There were no instances of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), active tuberculosis (TB), TB reactivation or serious hypersensitivity reactions.
safety.note: contRAst X: no PAP in 2915 patients over up to 2.5 years at the weekly regimen that sustained engagement.
safety.reason: No PAP below the neutralising threshold
safety.judgement: Largest exposure; the knockout scores this contra, the human model same, because its prediction is conditional on complete neutralisation that pharmacological dosing was not shown to reach. If a later source shows alveolar GM-CSF bioactivity was abolished at 150 mg weekly, this track turns contra. First comparison on the human-PAP otilimab sc track; BAROQUE (2020, no pulmonary events) is its earlier dataset but cannot be appended before it without breaking the track's year order.

safety.confidence_note: Protocol Amendment 02 (approved 2020-01-21, uploaded 2023-01-31), risk table pp. 20-21; the sentence runs across a page break in the PDF. Dose levels with and without the finding are said to exist but are given only in the Investigator Brochure.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13-week SC and 26-week IV GLP toxicology of otilimab (GSK3196165)
safety.quote: Non-adverse minimal to mild foamy alveolar macrophage accumulation were noted in lungs of monkeys in the 13-week SC and 26-week IV toxicology studies but were reversible following an off drug period.
safety.note: Otilimab itself gave monkeys reversible foamy alveolar macrophages, the PAP precursor, above a dose level; the margin is scored in dose.
safety.judgement: Untested rather than same: the species predicted the on-target lung change only above the NOEL, patients were never exposed there, and decision 16 counts the harm once, in the dose cell where the margin held. The prediction itself (foamy macrophages at supra-NOEL exposure) has no patient comparison.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Stanley 1994 (10.1073/pnas.91.12.5592) reported the same lung pathology plus subclinical lung infections in an independent knockout; Kitamura 1999 (10.1084/jem.190.6.875) showed neutralising anti-GM-CSF autoantibodies cause human PAP, the loss-of-function analogue in people.
safety.quote: Although steady-state hematopoiesis was unimpaired in homozygous mutant animals, all animals developed the progressive accumulation of surfactant lipids and proteins in the alveolar space, the defining characteristic of the idiopathic human disorder pulmonary alveolar proteinosis.
safety.note: Germline GM-CSF loss gives every mouse alveolar proteinosis and lung infection; every anti-GM-CSF trial then monitored lung function, KL-6 and surfactant protein D.
safety.judgement: Opening entry for the knockout x otilimab IV (MOR103) track at the model's first use.

safety.magnitude_basis: predicted alveolar proteinosis and lung infection in every animal; no pulmonary event of clinical concern in 222 patients dosed up to 50 weeks
safety.population: Active RA, Phase 1b/2a (MOR103 IV, four weekly doses; NCT01023256)
safety.confidence_note: Four weekly doses is short exposure for a slowly developing harm; Behrens 2015 OA full text read for the quote.
safety.quote: Surfactant D levels remained normal and there was no overall pattern of PFT alterations in MOR103-treated subjects.
safety.note: MOR103 Phase 1b/2a: SP-D normal and no pattern of PFT change after four weekly IV doses; the knockout's unconditional PAP did not appear.
safety.short: No SP-D or PFT signal, MOR103
safety.judgement: Split from safety 3 (checker verdict: earliest patient dataset that could show the harm). A predicted harm that did not appear is contra, opposite; low confidence for the short course.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Stanley 1994 (10.1073/pnas.91.12.5592) reported the same lung pathology plus subclinical lung infections in an independent knockout; Kitamura 1999 (10.1084/jem.190.6.875) showed neutralising anti-GM-CSF autoantibodies cause human PAP, the loss-of-function analogue in people.
safety.quote: Although steady-state hematopoiesis was unimpaired in homozygous mutant animals, all animals developed the progressive accumulation of surfactant lipids and proteins in the alveolar space, the defining characteristic of the idiopathic human disorder pulmonary alveolar proteinosis.
safety.note: Germline GM-CSF loss gives every mouse alveolar proteinosis and lung infection; every anti-GM-CSF trial then monitored lung function, KL-6 and surfactant protein D.
safety.judgement: Opening entry for the knockout x namilumab sc track at the model's first use.

safety.magnitude_basis: predicted alveolar proteinosis and lung infection in every animal; no pulmonary event of clinical concern in 222 patients dosed up to 50 weeks
safety.population: RA with inadequate response to methotrexate or one TNF inhibitor, background methotrexate in both arms (NEXUS)
safety.confidence_note: Taylor 2019 OA full text read for the quote; 12-week exposure.
safety.quote: With regard to change from baseline in biomarkers with the potential for early detection of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (carcinoembryonic antigen, KL-6, and SP-D), there were no trends associated with namilumab treatment.
safety.note: NEXUS: no trend in CEA, KL-6 or SP-D over 12 weeks of namilumab; the knockout's unconditional PAP did not appear.
safety.judgement: Split from safety 3 for the namilumab sc track. A predicted harm that did not appear is contra, opposite.
